corrections.ordered_by: "Fetch and put in the answer in out tokens from the run while the info exists.." (2026-10-23, on the lucene run's answer calls on the 715 whose rows held 0 tokens)
corrections.what_happened: On 600 answer calls the CLI's reply held 0 in its usage field and an empty list of iterations, while the same reply's counts per model and the CLI's own transcript of the call held the tokens. The harness reads the usage field, so the rows held 0 tokens for those calls.

rule.text:
1. An answer call (the row's call record marked role: answer) is corrected when its reply's usage
     field holds 0 tokens in and 0 out and its list of iterations is empty.
  2. Its counts are the reply's own counts per model (modelUsage), for the one model the call
     names, counted as the harness counts the usage field (harness.chat): tokens in = inputTokens
     + cacheCreationInputTokens + cacheReadInputTokens, cached tokens in = cacheReadInputTokens,
     tokens out = outputTokens.
  3. They must be the counts of the CLI's own transcript of the call, found by the reply's
     session_id; otherwise nothing is written.
  4. They go into the call record's usage and into the row's generator. The reply itself (the
     envelope) stays as the CLI wrote it; no answer, context, score or time changes.

not_changed_and_worth_knowing: Why the CLI wrote 0 in its usage field on these calls is not known. On them its list of iterations is empty, and they took longer: a median of 18.3 s against 5.4 s for the other answer calls.
No answer, context, score or time is changed: only the tokens of those answer calls.

checks.what: every answer call corrected has counts for its one model in its own reply
those counts are the CLI's own transcript of the call, by session_id

evidence.what: the CLI's own transcript counts of each corrected call, read on the machine that made the calls

corrections.what_happened: The two non-LLM context scores compared each gold record, written in HERB's own form, with the texts handed over, so the ids, labels, dates and names of the form were counted in how alike two records are.

before.what_it_did: each gold record in record_text form, against the texts as handed over, a text of several records (meta chunk_ids) cut into their record_text forms (eval/ragas.py as it stood uncommitted on 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-24, when the runs on the 715 answerable questions were scored)

rule.text:
1. The evaluation compared gold records and handed-over texts in two forms that are not the
     same. The code that scored the three final runs on the hundred wrote each gold record as all
     of its string values joined by spaces, while every arm hands its records over in HERB's own
     form (harness.record_text), with ids, labels, dates and names around the content, so the
     same record did not match itself as a string. The code that scored the runs on the 715
     answerable questions wrote each gold record in record_text form, so the ids, labels, dates
     and names of the form were counted in how alike two records are.
  2. The artefact hands over chunks of several records; a whole chunk was compared with single
     gold records and never matched one.
  3. Both sides are reduced to record content (harness.record_content): each gold record's
     content, against the content of each record handed over, every text cut into its records
     (eval.ragas.contents_handed_over).
  4. context_recall_nonllm and context_precision_nonllm are calculated again by RAGAS's own
     NonLLMContextRecall and NonLLMContextPrecisionWithReference on those contents; every other
     score and every other file stays as it is.

not_changed_and_worth_knowing: No answer, context, context_ids, other score or judge call is changed; arm_outputs.jsonl is as it was. The content is taken out only for these two scores; the answer model and the judge got the texts as they were handed over.
Content against content still counts different records as alike when their text is more than half the same, as HERB's templated Slack messages often are (output/research/2026-10-23-nonllm-checks).

corrections.what_happened: The run's starts recorded no code version: git gave no answer in the shell they ran in on the desktop. The commit each one ran on is the one its clone's HEAD named when it began, by the clone's own reflog.

rule.text:
1. A start (an entry of legs) is corrected when its code_version.commit is empty.
  2. Its commit is the one the clone's HEAD moved to last before the start's started_at, by the
     reflog, and its branch the one the reflog's last checkout before then moved to. dirty and
     code_state stay empty: whether the working copy differed from the commit, and how, is not
     recorded.
  3. A start that recorded its commit must be the commit rule 2 gives for it; otherwise nothing is
     written.
  4. The run's top-level code_version is its last start's, as the harness writes it.

not_changed_and_worth_knowing: Whether a start's working copy differed from its commit, and how, is not recorded: dirty and code_state stay empty. A start whose git answered may show that it did.

checks.what: rule 3: each start that recorded its commit is the commit the reflog gives for it

evidence.what: the clone's reflog, written on the machine that ran the starts
